Verdict

Reviewed 27 Oct 2026 · next 25 Jan 2027

Server-first parser sanitizer. Faster than DOMPurify-on-jsdom and far lighter than dragging in jsdom, but its defaults are aggressive: img and svg are removed unless you allow them. Zero executions in the harness; 17 historical advisories, all fixed, and the current release is clean.

Current Requirement: Sanitize untrusted HTML before rendering

Reasoning

  1. 0 of 25 vectors executed after sanitization; the control executed 11.
  2. About 400 sanitizations per second on a 60 KB document in Node, versus 49 for DOMPurify running on jsdom.
  3. Works without a DOM, which makes it the right choice for SSR and background jobs.
  4. 2.18.1 is clean in OSV and includes fixes for several October 2026 CVEs.
  5. Six direct dependencies install to 16 packages and 4.1 MB, versus 27.4 MB for jsdom.
  6. Default output escapes disallowed markup and drops dangerous tags entirely.

Caveats

  • Defaults drop img and svg. If you need images, add them to allowedTags explicitly; several historic advisories involved SVG and URI schemes.
  • No bundled types; you need @types/sanitize-html.
  • The standalone GitHub repository is archived. Source now lives in the Apostrophe monorepo, which makes targeted review harder.
  • 17 advisories, including a CRITICAL xmp passthrough fixed in 2.17.4 and an October 2026 SMIL bypass fixed in 2.18.0. Pin and update.
  • Manual npm publishing; no provenance.

Decision context

Approved

dompurify is the primary choice for Sanitize untrusted HTML before rendering. This package is classified as Adopted.

Use DOMPurify wherever a browser DOM is available, because parsing with the real DOM is the strongest defence against mutation XSS. Use sanitize-html for Node and SSR, where jsdom would add 27 MB for the same outcome. Use rehype-sanitize when content already flows through remark/rehype, which is the case for the assistant-ui react-markdown pipeline. Keep isomorphic-dompurify on hold: it is correct, but only worth its jsdom footprint if you need DOMPurify specifically on the server. Keep xss on hold: it is fast and safe in the harness, but its escape-not-strip model and lack of independent advisory coverage make it a weaker default. insane and sanitizer are abandoned and must not be used. No package in this category publishes npm provenance, so pin exact versions, subscribe to advisories for the chosen sanitizer, and re-review every 90 days. A 25-vector headless-Chrome corpus executed 11 vectors unsanitized and zero after every tested sanitizer.
